nodes.start.options.[splac].text.t: I'll pay it for you. You can give it back when you have it.

nodes.start.options.[umorz].text.t: You don't pay. The market woman writes off the debt, and I explain to her that it's worth her while.

nodes.start.options.[zastrasz].text.t: You pay by tomorrow or your stools go for firewood.

nodes.start.text.t: The debtor sits on a stool, sipping something from a mug. "Turnip sent you? That woman has an imagination. Debt? What debt? I only borrow, and she only thinks it's a debt. If you don't like it, go to the bailiff, if you can find him."

nodes.wynik_splac.text.t: Nail drinks in your words like a man dying of thirst. "Mister, you're a saint!" Before you know it he's bought you a tankard, but leaves the bill on your knee. The market woman gets her money, you get gratitude you can't spend.

nodes.wynik_umorz.text.t: Turnip stares at you in surprise, then at Nail, who suddenly looks like a man who's been pardoned. "All right, but only because you've got the gift of the gab." With a wave of her hand she wipes out four months of debt and two months of hatred.

nodes.wynik_zastrasz.text.t: Nail goes white as flour, puts down the glass and pulls a handkerchief-wrapped bundle of coins from his pocket. "You're brutal! But honest, because you say what you want." He pays to the last groat, and you feel as if you'd learned a new trade.
